name: Hephaestus
body:
HEPHAESTUS
CR 30

XP 6,881,200
CN Medium outsider (god)
Init +11; Senses blindsight 500 ft., darkvision 60 ft., true seeing; Perception +53

DEFENSE

AC 56, touch 28, flat-footed 56 (+19 armor, +9 shield, -1 Dex, +19 deflection)
hp 920 (40d10 +520)
Fort +36, Ref +23, Will + 34
DR 38/-; SR 41

OFFENSE

Speed 30ft. (20ft.)
Melee legendary reflecting heavy steel shield, crushing, flaming burst, legendary tether, supersonic, volcanic warhammer+58 (2d8+1d10 fire+ 1d6 fire +26)
Special Attacks Tools of the Gods
Spell-Like Abilities (CL 30th)
Domain Spells

9th–elemental swarm (fire only), prismatic sphere (DC 36) 8th- incendiary cloud, instant summons (DC 35)
7th–elemental body IV (fire only), wall of iron (DC 34) 6th- fire shield, major creation (DC 33)
5th–fabricate, fire shield (DC 32)
4th–minor creation, wall of fire (DC 31)
3rd–fireball, stone shape (DC 30)
2nd–produce flame, wood shape (DC 29)
1st–animate rope, burning hands (DC 28)
19/day–summon (any creatures, combined CR of 30 or less)

STATISTICS

Str 32, Dex 32, Con 34, Int 48, Wis 30, Cha 24 Base Atk +40; CMB +51; CMD +67
Feats Cleave, Combat Expertise, Deific Casting, Endurance, Great Cleave, Greater Fortitude, Greater Sunder, Improved Greater Fortitude, Improved Sunder, Legendary Magic, Power Attack, Quickdraw, Skill Focus Craft (alchemy), Skill Focus Craft (armor), Skill Focus Craft (bows), Skill Focus Craft (jewelry), Skill Focus Craft (ships), Skill Focus Craft (stonemasonry), Skill Focus Craft (weapons), Sundering Strike
Skills Appraise +62, Bluff +50, Craft (alchemy) +74, Craft (armor) +74, Craft (bows) +74, Craft (jewelry) +74, Craft (ships) +74, Craft (stonemasonry) +74, Craft (weapons) +74, Disable Device +42, Escape Artist +39, Heal +50, Knowledge (arcane) +59, Knowledge (engineering) +62, Knowledge (planes) +62, Knowledge (religion) +62, Perception +53, Profession (GM’s choice) +50, Ride +39, Sense Motive +53, Sleight of Hand +39, Spellcraft +59, Stealth +42, Use Magic Device +47
SQ Artifacts: crushing, flaming burst, legendary tether, supersonic, volcanic warhammer– cast titan maker once per day and add +15 to all damage rolls; +10 legendary full plate with +20 maximum Dex bonus that adds +5 to the DC of Lord of Gears and Artifice

Deific Traits: Lord of Ash and Flames

Deific Weaknesses: Fabled Flaw (Dexterity)

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Aligned Strike (Su)

A deity’s natural weapons, as well as any weapons it wields, are treated as being aligned to both sides of the deity’s alignment and as being epic for the purpose of resolving damage reduction.

Domain Mastery (Sp)

Hephaestus possesses the Artifice and Fire domains. He may use any domain powers and cast any spells associated with his domains at-will. Hephaestus counts as a 30th level cleric for the purposes of domain powers and casting spells.

Tools of the Gods (Su)

Hephaestus is the craftsman of the gods themselves. The swords and shields that shape and control the elemental forces of the world were all crafted in his forge, and a few of them never left his possession. The first attack Hephaestus makes with his weapon each round deals L-damage (DC 44), and Hephaestus’s armor allows him to double the damage reduction granted by his divinity score. Additionally, Hephaestus receives 1 additional divinity points when being created. These bonus divinity point must be spent on an artifact.

Lord of Gears and Artifice (Su)

Hephaestus is the father of all great weapons. Lesser creations dare not harm him. Once per round, if a character wishes to attack Hephaestus using a manufactured weapon or item (such as a sword, gun, staff, or wand), they must make a DC49 Will save or else their weapons rebel and refuse to attack Hephaestus. If the character fails this Will save, they may take other actions as normal, but they may not attack with any weapons. Creatures attacking as part of a full attack action who fail this Will save may not attempt to the attack the deity with any subsequent attacks.

Exploit Flaws (Ex)

Haphaestus can instantly identify even the most minute flaw in a weapon or piece of armor. For one as skilled and inveterate as Haphaestus, it’s a simple matter to use such slight flaws to utterly shatter the object. The first time each round that a creature is struck by a melee attack from Haphaestus, Haphaestus may immediately attempt to sunder one weapon or piece of armor worn or held by the creature as a free action.

Semi-Unlimited Wish (Sp)

The deity may cast unlimited wish once per day as a spell-like ability that does not require material components. The unlimited wish may only be in regards to something within the deity’s purview. A god of oceans could cause global draught or flooding, for instance, but could not produce any effect unrelated to oceans.

ECOLOGY

Environment any
Organization solitary
Treasure triple standard; +10 legendary full plate of heavy fortification and greater fire, cold, electricity, and acid resistance, with a +20 maximum Dex bonus that adds +5 to the DC of Lord of Gears and Artifice, +7 legendary reflecting heavy steel shield, crushing, flaming burst, legendary tether, supersonic, volcanic warhammer that allows the wielder to use the titan maker true dweomer once per day and adds +15 to all of the wielder’s damage rolls.

Gods have nice things. Lots of nice things. GMs wishing to have their players gain wealth as normal after fighting a deity can simply give their players triple the standard wealth they would normally obtain for an encounter of their level (plus any artifacts or other gear possessed by the deity.) However, GMs should keep in mind that players fighting CR 30 creatures are probably nearing the end of their campaigns, thus making how much wealth they receive less of a balancing factor, and that deities are likely to have accumulated quite a few extremely powerful magical items over the years. In other words, GMs are encouraged to add a little something extra to the loot pile after their players have defeated the gods. When you’ve managed to beat the snot out of a deity of war or have finally vanquished a not-so-eternal nemesis, they’ve earned a bonus. Don’t you think? A magnus stands at the head of his pantheon. Zeus, Odin, and Amun Ra may be known for far more than simply ruling, but their sway over the gods in their service gives them power over the laws of the universe that no other can claim. The personality of a magnus does far more than define him alone; it defines how the world itself stands. An evil magus can turn the world into an oppressive nightmare realm while a more benevolent deity might strive toward some utopian end. Whatever the case, a magnus’s word commands all the gods in a pantheon and all each of those gods commands. When a magnus makes a decree, it is the universe itself that listens.
